quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are tired while riding.
When you will slow down where other drivers don't expect it.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down where other drivers don't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than car brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing down in unexpected places, like the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you.

questions.question: What does a pennant-shaped sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign marks the start of a no passing zone.

questions.question: Why is riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle not recommended?

options.text: It is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
It is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
It is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does swerving a motorcycle require?

options.text: You should do it to avoid a hazard on a slippery road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lot of traction.
questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick maneuver that needs a lot of traction to do safely. Do not swerve on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to keep space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you?

options.text: It gives you more time to respond to hazards.
It prevents you from finding an escape route.
It gives you space to maneuver your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents you from finding an escape route.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and the vehicle ahead gives you time to respond to mistakes and room to maneuver. Space helps you, not prevents you from escaping.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over scored pavement. Ride slowly, keep steady throttle control, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: In a staggered formation, how far behind the leader should the third rider be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds
questions.explanation: The lead rider rides on the left side of the lane. The second rider stays two seconds behind on the right side. The third rider stays on the left side, four seconds behind the lead rider.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road indicate?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both when either brake lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter, applying the brake when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes, applying both when either brake lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. It applies braking pressure to both brakes when you use either lever. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders for a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in first gear.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down and stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if you need to.

questions.question: You may not need a large space cushion when:

options.text: You cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and other vehicles in bad conditions. Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: A good lane position helps you do everything except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position helps you see and be seen better, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: On the freeway, you see a "Merging traffic" sign. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
Speed up to prevent traffic jams.
Move to another lane, if it is safe, to let traffic enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if it is safe, to let traffic enter.
questions.explanation: On roads with two or more lanes, make room for vehicles entering. Move to another lane if nobody is driving next to you.

questions.question: This sign warns you are approaching:
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: A good lane position should do everything except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid wind blasts and blind spots, give you an escape route, and set up for turns. It should never put you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change in direction or narrowing of roadway.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a curve or narrow road ahead. You may see these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you are going. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Approach it slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases your motorcycle, shift down and slowly approach the dog. When you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: On a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold wind and rain.
Ride more than 12 hours every day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from cold wind and rain.
questions.explanation: To stay safe on a long trip, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day. Take rest breaks at least every two hours. Do not use caffeine or stimulants. These cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: What should you do if the throttle gets stuck?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, twist it back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the new rider lead the group.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge how far away the motorcycle is and how fast it is going.

questions.question: What is the difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around and go in the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders who do not wear helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets. This is true at any speed.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, what should you do first?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, first try twisting it back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will properly yield to you.
It guarantees they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still do not see them.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting to first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your brakes to slow down before downshifting.
questions.explanation: Before shifting into a lower gear, slow down enough to shift safely. Downshifting at too high a speed can cause the motorcycle to lurch and the rear wheel to skid. When riding downhill or shifting to first gear, use the brakes to reach a safe speed before downshifting.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle on the left, where should you position yourself in your lane?

options.text: Move to the right part of your lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of your lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave back and forth in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of your lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Move to the left part of your lane before passing. This helps you see better and makes you more visible to other drivers. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding in a group and taking a curve, what formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single file.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when taking a curve. Groups normally ride in staggered formation, but switch to single file for curves, turns, entering highways, and leaving highways.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, how should you secure it?

options.text: Secure it as low as possible.
Secure it as high as possible.
Attach it to the sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure it as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can throw off your balance.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Try to accelerate while the brake is engaged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if the rear brake locks on a surface with good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Winding road with many turns ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when wet and is harder to drive on safely.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten the bike, square the handlebars, then stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten the bike, square the handlebars, then stop.
questions.explanation: Straighten and square the handlebars first, then stop. If you cannot straighten the bike, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually while reducing your lean angle.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Use the rear brake hard while slowly increasing front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop quickly.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket while riding in hot weather, what should you do?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on.
questions.explanation: Always wear a riding jacket for crash protection, regardless of weather. Jackets protect you from dehydration in hot weather and many are designed to prevent overheating.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run along your lane, at what angle should you approach them?
questions.correctAnswerText: 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks at a 45-degree angle. Then make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing at a shallow angle can catch your tires and throw you off balance.

questions.question: How do you achieve maximum braking power in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time without locking either wheel to achieve maximum straight-line braking.
